column1: # gentoo-install — package set inheritance
# This file is the inheritance table. It is data, not a comment in a script,
# because the question a reader actually asks is "what does desktop add over
# server" and the answer has to be readable without opening any code
# (DESIGN.md §10).
#     base ──▶ minimal ──▶ server ──▶ desktop
# Each level adds to the one before it and removes nothing. Resolving a set
# means walking the inherits column up to the root and concatenating the
# .list files from the root down, so a package named twice is installed once
# and the order stays readable in the generated Portage set.
# The two init sets are not part of that chain. They are overlaid on whatever
# level was chosen, according to --init, because the answer to "what provides
# cron and the system log" is the one thing the init system genuinely decides.
# Every set has a data/packages/<set>.list beside this file, and each of those
# files repeats its parent in an "# inherits: <parent>" header. The installer
# cross-checks the two and complains if they drift.
# columns: set
base
column3: Portage tooling and hardware inventory: the packages every install gets
